frontier.hypothesis: The original initPolyG4 prototype RETURNED the primitive pointer (u8 *initPolyG4(u8 *) or void *initPolyG4(void), PsyQ-chaining style), which changes the post-call block's live-in set and, critically, occupies $v0 at block entry - and $v0 being free is the measured reason our 640 constant lands there instead of $v1 with a long live range.
frontier.mechanism: s3 proved the residual is hard-register reuse: local-alloc gives the 640 pseudo $v0 because $v0 is dead from the 128 constant's last use onward, and the resulting REG_DEP_OUTPUT pins the li. s3's attempts to occupy $v0 by extending ANOTHER constant's live range failed (6/11/11) because sched1 re-collapses the 640 set past the extender. A call RETURN value is different in kind: it is defined by the call insn itself (before any block insn, so sched1 cannot sink anything above it) and it lives in $v0 by ABI, so if the stores are written through the returned pointer the $v0 lifetime spans the whole block at zero extra instructions. This is the only measured-relevant lever (register pressure at block entry) that the s5 search space cannot express, because the search fixed the extern's signature.
frontier.next_probe: First establish the prototype honestly: grep every caller of initPolyG4 in src/ and read the target asm of two or three of them (asm/funcs/) to see whether any consumes $v0 after the jal - if the original returned a value, some caller will use it, and if none does the hypothesis dies immediately and cheaply. If it survives, declare 'extern u8 *initPolyG4(u8 *p);' and write the body as 'p = initPolyG4((u8 *)D_800A38B4);' (and the variant that keeps the argument copy), then score with s5/scoreforms.py, watching the constant signature and the sh v1,16 slot separately. NB: changing a shared extern's signature is a tree-wide edit, so verify no other caller's codegen regresses (sandbox those callers) before proposing it - and it is only credible if the callers' asm supports it, otherwise it is a coercion dressed as an interface.

frontier.hypothesis: No matched function in the tree emits a block-head constant whose only uses lie AFTER an intervening may-alias-pinned load - which would mean the original source did not have the OT-base load between the 640 set and its uses at all, and lever L1's in-block position (correct as an emission position) is being produced by the wrong source construct.
frontier.mechanism: s4's census found 164 matched functions with a block-head 'addiu $vN,$zero,K' whose first use is >= 4 insns later, but it did NOT filter on what sits between the set and the first use. The one hit that was read (func_80072BC4) has an uninterrupted store run, and s4 recorded that interruption as the concrete difference. If the filtered census returns ZERO interrupted-run instances across 1400 functions, the interruption is not something GCC 2.7.2 tolerates, and the source must be producing the lui/lw from somewhere our forms cannot reach by moving the statement inside the block - e.g. the OT slot address computed into a local BEFORE the initPolyG4 call (a pre-call lw, out of the store run entirely) with something else accounting for target's mid-block lui/lw pair.
frontier.next_probe: Extend tmp/grind/func_8003553C/s4/census.py with the extra predicate 'at least one non-store insn between the constant's set and its first use' and re-run over all matched functions; report the count and, if non-zero, read the C of every hit with offset/limit Reads. Then, independently of the census result, measure the two source shapes the s2/s5 sweeps never covered because they only moved the load WITHIN the post-call block: (i) 'ot' computed from D_800A374C BEFORE the initPolyG4 call, (ii) the OT base read before the call with the +0x401C displacement applied inside the block. Score both with s5/scoreforms.py and record the emitted position of the lui/lw pair, not just difflines.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual store's slot is decided by sched2 (post-RA), not sched1, so the decisive dump to read is the sched2 ready-list state for the two candidate insns rather than any further source enumeration.
frontier.mechanism: s3 traced the 640 set through combine/sched/lreg/greg/sched2 for the HOLDER form (both stores late), but never traced the INCUMBENT (leading store), which is the form that is one instruction away. In the incumbent the constant already has target's register and slot, so whatever displaces sh v1,16(s0) by 17 slots is a decision taken with the allocation already correct - a genuinely different question from the one s3 answered, and it can only be read out of the dumps, not guessed from scores.
frontier.next_probe: Run tmp/grind/func_8003553C/s3/rtl.sh on the INCUMBENT body to get its full cc1 -da pass set, then compare base.i.sched2's dependence and priority state for the sh v1,16 insn against the corresponding insn in the holder form's dumps (rtl_B/, already on disk). Identify which dependence or priority term makes the incumbent's store schedulable at index 13 and whether any source-level construct removes that term without disturbing the constant's allocation. Report the term explicitly in the ledger even if no lever follows - naming it converts the remaining search from enumeration to targeting.
